subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Does the current audit or history query surface expose a remotely reachable resource-exhaustion path that warrants additional server-side limits despite the reported recursive-filter primitive being absent?
rationale: Selecting rate limits, execution deadlines, or stricter query bounds depends on the intended trust model and acceptable administrative-query behavior, which cannot be safely inferred from the unconfirmed report.

options.title: Close after confirmation
options.body: Confirm that the named paths accept only bounded scalar queries and close the report as based on a nonexistent filter contract.

options.title: Request concrete reproduction
options.body: Ask for the exact route or RPC payload, authentication context, query plan, and measured CPU or lock impact on current main.

options.title: Adopt bounded hardening
options.body: If review finds a reachable expensive query, add fixed server-side cost and concurrency bounds with regression and abuse proof.

recommendation.title: Close after confirmation
recommendation.body: Confirm that the named paths accept only bounded scalar queries and close the report as based on a nonexistent filter contract.
